title: Handover quicklog ritual - October 19 2026
content:
Context:
This is the quick-handover note from the 2300-0700 watch (UTC) on 2026-10-19. Primary focus tonight: a transient p95 latency surge affecting inference-router and a small spike in 429s coming from the batching-service. No customer-impacting outage; some degraded tail latency for a small slice of requests (~0.6% of traffic) during the peak window.

Summary (top-line):
- Window: 2026-10-19 01:12 - 2026-10-19 02:04 UTC (main anomalies), residual noise until ~02:20 UTC.
- Symptoms: p95 for inference-router rose from baseline ~210ms to ~880ms for ~52 minutes. 429s from batching-service increased from baseline 0.02% to 0.8% for that window. No error-rate increase in model-hosts; token-generation steady.
- Incident ID (internal): INC-2026-10-19-01
- Severity: Sev3 (customer-facing latency but limited population and short lived).

Timeline (concise):
- 01:10 UTC: Alert fires - monitor alerted on sustained p95 > 700ms for 10m across us-west-2 inference-router cluster.
- 01:12 UTC: Pager -> me (Evan). Slack thread opened in #sre-ops.
- 01:15 UTC: Quick triage: dashboards show queuing on batching-service; CPU on autoscaler nodes normal, but queue depth on Redis-KV (prefix-cache) elevated for certain routing keys.
- 01:20 UTC: Deployed short-lived debug snapshot to inference-router (extra logging) and enabled trace sampling on a sample route (route: /v1/generate-chat).
- 01:28 UTC: Identified a coordination stall between batching-service and cache invalidation loop — a recent cron job for prefix-warmup (deploy earlier today) accidentally started a runaway warmup for one customer keyspace, causing many small cache writes and eviction pressure.
- 01:32 UTC: Disabled warmup cron for suspect keyspace (immediate drop in write pressure observed).
- 01:38 UTC: 429s fall back towards baseline; p95 starts decreasing but remains elevated due to backlog processing.
- 02:04 UTC: p95 returns to baseline; kept watch until 02:20 UTC for residual tail events.

Root cause hypothesis:
- Primary: runaway prefix-warmup job (deployed earlier in the day by solutions-engineering) iterated aggressively over a heavy customer keyspace. That job produced a high write+eviction rate on Redis that increased batching-service request latency (requests waiting on KV cache ops and eviction churn). Secondary amplification from a routing policy that pinned some high-QPS customers to a small subset of inference-router pods (config drift in routing table).
- Contributing: warmup job lacked a hard rate-limit; monitoring alert for cache-evictions not enabled for the keyspace.

Mitigation applied tonight:
- Disabled the warmup cron for the offending keyspace (Rohit).
- Throttled batching-service client requeue to drop aggressive retry storm (short-term change in feature flag).
- Increased trace sampling to collect 1:50 for the route and captured 12 traces (linked artifact).

Runbook / Playbook notes (edits to propose):
- Add a pre-check to any prefix-warmup job: compute expected write ops per second (wops/s) given keyspace size and abort if > X threshold (proposal: 200 wops/s).
- Add an alert for unexpected Redis eviction rate per prefix namespace (new metric: redis.evictions.namespace.*).
- Document emergency kill-switch for warmup crons (single API toggle + on-call runbook step).
- Update the routing-policy CI to ensure even distribution across inference-router pods for high-QPS customers; add a Canary gate for routing-table changes.

Metrics snapshot (observed during peak):
- inference-router p95: baseline 210ms -> peak 880ms -> baseline by 02:04 UTC
- 429 rate (batching-service): baseline 0.02% -> 0.8% peak -> 0.03% post-mitigation
- redis evictions (global): baseline ~1.1k/min -> peak 11.8k/min during warmup job
- queue depth (batching internal queue): avg baseline 4 -> peaked at 72 per worker

Action items (short):
1) Rohit: Draft a rate-limiting guard for prefix-warmup jobs and open PR to infra repo. Due: 2026-10-21. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1234 (WIP).
2) Aisha: Add redis.evictions.namespace.* metric and dashboard panel, plus alert with 10m window. Due: 2026-10-22.
3) Marcus: Add routing-policy CI check + unit test to catch hard pinning of customers. Due: 2026-10-23.
4) Evan (me): Write short post-mortem draft and link artifacts, assign postmortem owner. Due: 2026-10-22.
5) Oncall: Confirm warmup cron toggle is exposed on ops-console with RBAC. Follow-up with Solutions Eng. (assigned to Solutions Eng owner SRE-ops loop).

Owners and contacts:
- Oncall owner (this shift): Evan Morales (pager) - slack: @evan.m
- SRE lead for infra: Aisha Patel - slack: @aisha
- Solutions-eng contact (warmup job author): Rohit Banerjee - slack: @rohit
- Routing-policy owner: Marcus Liu - slack: @marcus

Open follow-ups for next shift (priority order):
- [P0] Lock-in immediate guard for warmup jobs (Rohit + infra review). Blocker for preventing recurrence.
- [P1] Add eviction metric + alert (Aisha). Verify dashboard and run alert test with synthetic warmup.
- [P2] Routing CI + configuration audit for high-QPS customers (Marcus). Run audit across last 30 days.
- [P3] Postmortem and timeline expansion (Evan). Draft with links to traces and logs.
- [P4] Decide on long-term strategy: either move warmup to a separate isolated Redis cluster for large customers OR introduce per-namespace write quotas. (Discussion @eng-arch.)

Notes to next shift:
- Residual telemetry is normal; no ongoing elevated user errors observed. Watch for elevated redis.evictions.namespace.* if present (we added a temporary aggregator rule to the monitoring config for the keyspace).
- Batch-service feature-flag throttle is temporary and will revert after we have rate-limiter PR merged. If you see elevated backpressure after revert, escalate to Marcus and Aisha.
- Deployment tags used in tracing: infra-warmup-2026-10-19 and batching-throttle-flag-2026-10-19.

Quick debugging artifacts:
- Collected traces: 12 traces attached to incident (link in Jira: SRE-4812).
- Redis slowlog excerpt: included in incident notes.
- Short-term debug deployment logs: available in ops-artifacts bucket path: s3://ops-artifacts/sre/incidents/2026-10-19-INC-2026-10-19-01/logs.zip

Retrospective suggestions (for retro):
- Run a fault-injection job quarterly that simulates a warmup at different scales to ensure autoscaler and cache eviction metrics behave in expected envelopes.
- Create a lightweight checklist for solutions-engineering before launching warmup jobs (owner sign-off + metrics guard).

Pager coverage / rotation note:
- Next oncall: Priya Desai (starting 0700 UTC). I added a short handover note in the rotation calendar and pinged @priyaa in #sre-ops.

Final:
- No customer tickets opened directly because we did not see user-visible errors; Solutions Eng has been informed and will reach out to the customer whose keyspace was involved to explain the incident and the safe guards being added.

If anything looks off first hour after takeover: escalate to SRE lead Aisha and page Marcus if routing policy oddities reappear.

-- Evan Morales
Oncall 2300-0700 UTC, 2026-10-19
